da-overclaim.evidence: The .md claims the knot-type eigenbasis of V_phys = colim V^⊗n 'is complete'. Naming the two n=3 channel values makes a counter-fact reachable and it is now Lean-proved: they COINCIDE at q ≈ 0.779544663820934968877573423932 (both ≈ -2.0623447988, verified 50 dps), a q the Descartes condition permits (0 < q, q ≠ 1). See `jonesSymmetric_eq_jonesMixed_iff` (the reduction to q^5 - q^4 + q^3 + q^2 - 1 = 0, proved not asserted), `jones_channels_coincide` (IVT root in [7/10, 4/5]) and `jones_channels_not_separating`. So exhibiting two non-zero channel values does not establish that the two summands are DISTINGUISHED, which is what completeness needs.
da-overclaim.notes: Scope-(a) per AGENTS: this is a negative about the n=3 pair of Jones values as a separator, not a refutation of eigenbasis completeness — separation may hold via trSummand, whose per-summand character values for general n are upstream and not in this file. Recorded in the module docstring.

da-overclaim.evidence: Supersedes my own warn of 2026-09-04. That entry said naming the two n=3 Jones values exposed a counter-fact (they coincide at q* ~ 0.7795446638) and treated the general-n per-summand character values as an upstream gap. The gap claim was WRONG: chi^lambda for general n and lambda is live in tools/hecke-engine/src/seminormal.rs (Hoefsmit) with MPFR variants and ~20 Python entry points via pyhecke_native 0.9.0. Measured with chi_lambdas_braid_mpfr at 50 dps: the characters separate the two summands on all 5 words tested AT q* itself, and the closed forms chi^[3](s1) = q, chi^[2,1](s1) = q - 1/q give difference 1/q, verified at 8 sample q to < 1e-45.
da-overclaim.notes: So jones_channels_not_separating is a narrow negative about the pair those theorems named, not about the framework. Positive counterpart now Lean-proved beside it: `sigma_separates_n3_channels` — sigma_1 separates at every Descartes q, since q > 0 forces q^-1 != 0. Probe: computations/descartes_n3_channel_separation_probe.py + witness. Bean qou-qhs3. Still genuinely open, and it is formalisation not mathematics: constructing trSummand from the Hoefsmit values in Lean.
